summary: Home health EHR with referral intake, visit-note drafting, scheduling, and coding review.
editor_note: Home health documentation needs a handoff, not just a transcript. Enzo brings eFax and portal referrals into intake, drafts OASIS-ready visit notes, and lets clinicians edit and sign before submission. Unlike a standalone scribe, it connects that work to coding review and now markets an EHR. Its module pages still promise existing-EHR integration, so agencies need to confirm the deployment scope and retain clinical judgment.
investors: N47, Gradient, Tandem Ventures, Rigby Watts

sources.label: Enzo QA review and override workflow
Commonwealth Home Care coding workflow and scope

product_evidence.claim: The current homepage offers a home health EHR spanning referral intake, scheduling, visit notes, coding, and claims, with agency staff reviewing and approving its work.
Intake collects referrals from eFax, hospital portals, and uploads; it checks package information and tracks an owner, status, and activity history before handing accepted referrals to scheduling.
Scribe describes drafting OASIS-ready notes from visit conversations and capturing medication-label information. Clinicians review, edit, and sign off before notes are submitted.
QA checks documentation and coding consistency, explains flagged issues, and allows coders or clinical reviewers to confirm, adjust, or override suggestions before submission.

The Commonwealth case describes AI-assisted ICD coding backed by certified coding reviewers; OASIS review remains with the agency's own team. Unsupported codes trigger requests for clinician clarification.

market_context.primary_user: Home health agency administrators, intake coordinators, visiting clinicians, and coding/QA staff managing referrals through documentation and billing review.
market_context.category: Home health EHR and clinical documentation workflows
market_context.differentiation: It joins referral intake, OASIS-oriented note drafting, and human coding review in a home-health-specific workflow rather than supplying a general-purpose visit transcript.
market_context.why_now: The public offer now includes an EHR alongside existing-EHR modules; agencies can evaluate workflow consolidation, but must establish which integration or replacement path is actually offered.

risks.claim: The homepage proposes replacing a legacy EHR, while module pages promise integration. Supported EHRs, migration effort, pricing, and contractual scope need confirmation for each agency.
risks.basis: VentureDex assessment of the homepage and Intake, Scribe, and QA pages; no agency implementation or commercial quote reviewed.

risks.claim: Generated notes and code suggestions still need qualified human review. The reviewed pages do not establish diagnostic accuracy, clinical efficacy, or guaranteed reimbursement improvements.
risks.basis: Scribe requires clinician sign-off; QA permits overrides; the Commonwealth case uses coding reviewers. Public workflow review, not clinical validation.
